raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds `decoupled_async`, a v1 trainer mode in which the trainer never drives rollout. The trainer only publishes weight versions and enqueues prompts in TransferQueue. Each vLLM replica pulls new versions with one-sided reads and decides on its own when to load them, and a rollout-side dispatcher starts enqueued prompts once replicas have the weights they require.

In `separate_async` today, every step ends with `CheckpointEngineManager.update_weights`: abort all requests, release KV, build a topology, push weights, resume. The trainer waits for it and every replica pauses at once. In `decoupled_async` the trainer's per-step weight work is a copy into a host slot; replicas prefetch while generating and pause only to load (~1 s at 0.5B, ~1.5 s at 8B).

Design doc: `docs/advance/decoupled_weight_sync.md`.

**Related work and why this is not a duplicate.** #8395 (`sharded_nixl`) moves only each rollout rank's TP/EP slice with NIXL writes, but stays trainer-pushed inside `CheckpointEngineManager`. #7108 is Megatron→SGLang P2P over Mooncake, also trainer-driven. #8168 adds standalone replica lifecycle APIs. This PR changes who drives the sync (rollout pulls on its own schedule) and removes the trainer's calls into rollout; it transfers full tensors. #8395's slice planning is the natural next step for sharded pulls on top of this.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: [decoupled weight sync](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+decoupled+weight+sync), [transport_pull](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+transport_pull), [prompt dispatcher](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+prompt+dispatcher), [torch.distributed._transport](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+torch.distributed._transport)
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

### Test

Hardware: one node, 8× H100 80GB SXM (NVLink, no InfiniBand), `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0` (NVLS multicast is unavailable on that VM). verl's locked env (torch 2.13, vLLM 0.32) unless noted.

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/trainer/ppo/v1/ tests/checkpoint_engine/test_weight_update_agent_on_cpu.py tests/checkpoint_engine/test_transport_pull_on_cpu.py tests/checkpoint_engine/test_transport_registry_on_cpu.py` (includes the new prompt dispatcher, decoupled_async and replay-buffer tests) | 269 passed |
| `pytest tests/checkpoint_engine/test_transport_pull_on_gpu.py` (torch 2.15 + nixl 1.5.2, both `nixl` and `nixl_native`) | 4 passed |
| `pytest tests/checkpoint_engine/test_correctness_on_gpu.py -k transport_pull` (FSDP Qwen3-8B → 6 mock rollout workers, 3 syncs, weights checked; torch 2.15) | passed for both transports |
| `pytest tests/utils/test_bucketed_weight_transfer.py -k IPC` | 8 passed |
| `pytest tests/workers/rollout/rollout_vllm/test_vllm_weight_update_agent.py` (real vLLM replica, versions 0→1→2 under load) | 1 passed |

End-to-end async GRPO on GSM8K (`tests/special_e2e/run_v1_separate_async.sh`, 4 train + 4 rollout GPUs, one seed), `separate_async` + `nccl` against `decoupled_async`:

| | `separate_async` + `nccl` | `decoupled_async` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, 30 steps: validation accuracy at steps 10 / 20 / 30 | 0.079 / 0.438 / 0.477 | 0.327 / 0.456 / 0.501 |
| 0.5B: step time / trainer time in `update_weights` | 5.80 s / 1.26 s | 4.74 s / 0.14 s |
| Qwen3-8B-Base, 20 steps, `bypass_mode=True`: validation accuracy at steps 0 / 10 / 20 | 0.638 / 0.870 / 0.896 | 0.644 / 0.860 / 0.887 |
| 8B: step time / trainer waiting for samples | 4.78 s / 0.05 s | 6.08 s / 2.47 s |
| `off_policy/trajectory_spans/mean` (both sizes) | 1.0 | 1.0 |

Accuracy matches within single-seed noise, and every trajectory is generated by a single weight version. Before the prompt dispatcher existed (weights pulled, prompts pushed by the trainer), 1.8–2.0 versions per trajectory were typical because prompts dispatched right after a publish were aborted and re-prefilled. Performance is not optimized yet: at 8B a replica update (full-copy pulls through host memory, ~6.3 s) is longer than a training step, so prompts wait for it; the NCCL baseline moves the 16 GB in 1.35 s. `min_version_lag=2` does not help (5.60 s per step), and admitting prompts on older weights would only get them aborted by the next update. Sharded pulls are the fix and are left for a follow-up; the goal here is separating rollout from the training loop.

### API and Usage Example

```bash
bash tests/special_e2e/run_v1_separate_async.sh \
    trainer.v1.trainer_mode=decoupled_async \
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.checkpoint_engine.backend=transport_pull \
    algorithm.rollout_correction.bypass_mode=True
```

New config (all additive): `trainer.v1.decoupled_async.{num_warmup_batches, parameter_sync_step, min_version_lag, poll_interval, init_timeout, max_inflight_prompts, dispatch_poll_interval}` and `checkpoint_engine.engine_kwargs.transport_pull.{device, transport, num_slots, rollout_dtype, lease_ttl, registry_name}`. The `transport_pull` backend also works under the existing `CheckpointEngineManager` flow.

### Design & Code Changes

Weight transfer, `verl/checkpoint_engine/transport/`:

- `registry.py`: directory of published versions (READY → RETIRED → reclaimed) with TTL reader leases judged on the registry's clock; a named Ray actor scoped to the job.
- `publisher.py`: the last `num_slots` versions live in pinned host buffers registered once; a slot is overwritten only after every lease on its version ends. fp32 weights are cast to `rollout_dtype` (bf16) on the way in.
- `puller.py`: leases a version, reads all buckets into a local registered mirror, and rejects the copy if the lease lapsed mid-read.
- `nixl_native.py`, `transport.py`: transports. `nixl_native` uses NIXL's bindings and runs on any torch; other names go to `torch.distributed._transport` (torch >= 2.15, which released vLLM does not support yet).
- `engine.py`: the `transport_pull` checkpoint engine (`send_weights` publishes, `prefetch`, `receive_weights`).
- `update_agent.py`: `WeightUpdateAgent`, one per vLLM replica. It prefetches a newer version while generating, then aborts in-flight requests, releases KV, loads the mirror, restores KV and resumes.

Trainer, `verl/trainer/ppo/v1/`:

- `trainer_decoupled_async.py`: publishes at init and step end, enqueues prompts with a `min_weight_version` tag, and on resume only resets interrupted prompts to `pending`. Before validation, which bypasses the dispatcher, it waits for every replica to serve the newest version. It makes no calls that control rollout (24 in `separate_async`).
- `prompt_dispatcher.py`: one per rollout service; claims pending prompts oldest first, up to `max_inflight_prompts`, once every replica has their version, and starts them on the agent loop workers.
- `standalone_rollout.py`: `StandaloneRolloutMixin` with what `separate_async` and `decoupled_async` share (standalone replicas, `DetachActorWorker`, Decoupled PPO old log-probs), moved verbatim out of `separate_async`.
- `replay_buffer.py`: in `decoupled_async`, a group's age for off-policy control (eviction, its metrics, and `sample()`'s assertion) is measured from the oldest weight version its trajectories started on; other modes keep the enqueue step. An optional `health_check_fn` runs on every poll so a failed agent or dispatcher fails the job instead of leaving `sample()` waiting.

Other fixes found along the way:

- `bucketed_weight_transfer.py`: weights larger than the bucket that arrive in host memory are staged on the GPU before CUDA IPC (`reduce_tensor` on a CPU tensor yields a shared-memory handle that `rebuild_ipc` cannot rebuild). Hit by Qwen3-8B's 1.24 GB embedding. The staged copy is returned to the device after the receiver acks. This also affects `nixl` with `device=cpu`.
- `CheckpointEngineWorker.prefetch_weights` for engines that support prefetching.

Review findings addressed since the first revision: the missing `on_sample_end` hook; pinned host buffers on CPU-only machines; fencing device-to-host copies before a version is announced; releasing the lease when a read fails; one staleness clock across eviction and `sample()`; syncing replicas before validation; the update agent loading the first version regardless of `min_version_lag`; counting rollout GPUs in throughput; the `separate_async` config comment.

Follow-ups (see the design doc): `keep` pause mode, version-aware routing, sharded pulls, a run epoch for resume once the registry outlives the job, reclaiming prompts from dead agent loop workers.

### Checklist Before Submitting

If not feasible, explain why: the new `*_on_cpu.py` tests (transport, registry, update agent, prompt dispatcher, decoupled_async, replay buffer) run in the CPU workflow. ** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Fix: `pin_memory=True` breaks the CPU-only CI job.** The `cpu_unit_tests` job fails in `test_publish_then_pull_is_bit_exact`. `torch.empty(..., pin_memory=True)` raises `RuntimeError` when no accelerator backend is present. The test uses `device="cpu"` with `_FakeTransport`, so it needs no pinned memory. Pin the buffer only when an accelerator is available. `WeightPuller._setup` in `puller.py` has the same allocation. Put the fix in one shared helper, for example in `transport.py`, and use it in both files.
🐛 Proposed fix

** Major** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Quick win** **Fix: missing device synchronize when `device == "cpu"` and the source tensors are on a GPU.** `copy_(..., non_blocking=True)` from a CUDA tensor into a pinned host slot is asynchronous. `TransportPullCheckpointEngine` defaults to `device="cpu"`. The trainer's `get_per_tensor_param` yields GPU tensors. The `self.device != "cpu"` check skips the synchronize in this case. `registry.publish` then announces the version while D2H copies can still be in flight. A reader can pull partially written weights. The lease fence does not detect this, because the publisher is the one writing. Synchronize whenever any source tensor is not on CPU.
🐛 Proposed fix
```diff --- "a/verl/checkpoint_engine/transport/publisher.py" +++ "b/verl/checkpoint_engine/transport/publisher.py" @@ -161,8 +161,8 @@ index += 1 if index != len(self.tensors): raise ValueError(f"Got {index} weights, layout has {len(self.tensors)}") - if self.device != "cpu": + if needs_sync: get_torch_device().synchronize() slot.version = version manifest = WeightManifest( ``` Also add `needs_sync = False` before the `async for` loop. Inside the loop, add `needs_sync |= tensor.device.type != "cpu"`. For a CUDA slot device, keep the synchronize unconditional: `needs_sync = needs_sync or self.device != "cpu"`.

On subsequent publishes with the default `device="cpu"` and CUDA-backed weights, `copy_(tensor, non_blocking=True)` queues asynchronous transfers into the pinned host slot, but this condition skips synchronization because the destination is on CPU. +import logging
+import os
+import time

+import torch
+
+from verl.utils.device import get_torch_device
+from verl.workers.rollout.utils import ensure_async_iterator
+
+from .registry import BucketDesc, WeightManifest, WeightRegistry
+from .transport import TransportFactory, bucket_ranges, default_transport_factory, plan_layout, tensor_view
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

+@dataclass
+class _Slot:
+    buffer: torch.Tensor
+    memories: list
+    buckets: list[BucketDesc]
+    version: int | None = None
+
+
+class WeightPublisher:
+    """Keeps the last `num_slots` weight versions in registered buffers that readers pull from.
+
+    Each slot holds a full copy of the model laid out by `plan_layout`, and each bucket-sized
+    range of a slot is registered once, on the first publish. Publishing a version writes into a
+    slot whose previous version no reader holds a lease on, then announces it in the registry
+    and retires older versions. The trainer never waits for readers beyond that.
+
+    Device memory overhead is `num_slots * model bytes` on `device`, counted in `rollout_dtype`.
+
+    Args:
+        registry: Where versions are announced.
+        bucket_size: Size in bytes of one remote read.
+        device: Device of the slot buffers, "cuda" or "cpu" (pinned host memory).
+        backend: torch.distributed._transport backend.
+        num_slots: Versions kept at once; 2 lets readers finish v while v+1 is written.
+        rollout_dtype: fp32 weights (e.g. FSDP master weights) are cast to this as they are copied
+            into a slot, halving slot memory and transfer for bf16. Other dtypes pass through.
+            None sends weights as the trainer produces them.
+        reclaim_timeout: Seconds to wait for leases on the slot being overwritten to end.
+        transport_factory: Override of transport construction, for tests.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        registry: WeightRegistry,
+        bucket_size: int,
+        device: str = "cuda",
+        backend: str = "nixl",
+        num_slots: int = 2,
+        rollout_dtype: torch.dtype | None = torch.bfloat16,
+        reclaim_timeout: float = 600.0,
+        transport_factory: TransportFactory = default_transport_factory,
+    ):
+        assert num_slots >= 1
+        self.registry = registry
+        self.bucket_size = bucket_size
+        self.device = device
+        self.backend = backend
+        self.num_slots = num_slots
+        self.rollout_dtype = rollout_dtype
+        self.reclaim_timeout = reclaim_timeout
+        self.transport_factory = transport_factory
+
+        self.transport = None
+        self.endpoint = None
+        self.tensors = None
+        self.total_bytes = None
+        self.slots: list[_Slot] = []
+
+    def _wire_dtype(self, dtype: torch.dtype) -> torch.dtype:
+        return self.rollout_dtype if self.rollout_dtype is not None and dtype == torch.float32 else dtype
+
+    def _setup(self, named_tensors: list[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]):
+        self.tensors, self.total_bytes = plan_layout(
+            [(n, t.shape, self._wire_dtype(t.dtype)) for n, t in named_tensors]
+        )
+        self.transport = self.transport_factory(self.backend, self.device)
+        ranges = bucket_ranges(self.total_bytes, self.bucket_size)
+        for _ in range(self.num_slots):
+            if self.device == "cpu":
+                buffer = torch.empty(self.total_bytes, dtype=torch.uint8, pin_memory=True)
+            else:
+                buffer = torch.empty(self.total_bytes, dtype=torch.uint8, device=self.device)
+            memories = [self.transport.register_memory(buffer[offset : offset + size]) for offset, size in ranges]
+            self.slots.append(_Slot(buffer=buffer, memories=memories, buckets=[]))
+        # Bind after registering: some backends (nixl_native) put registrations in the url.
+        self.endpoint = self.transport.bind()
+        for slot in self.slots:
+            slot.buckets = [
+                BucketDesc(offset=offset, size=size, remote_buffer=memory.to_remote_buffer().serialize())
+                for (offset, size), memory in zip(ranges, slot.memories, strict=True)
+            ]
+        logger.info(f"Publisher at {self.endpoint!r}: {self.num_slots} slots of {self.total_bytes} bytes")
+
+    async def _acquire_slot(self) -> _Slot:
+        """Pick the free slot, or the one holding the oldest version, and wait until no one reads it."""
+        slot = min(self.slots, key=lambda s: -1 if s.version is None else s.version)
+        if slot.version is None:
+            return slot
+        await self.registry.retire(slot.version)
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + self.reclaim_timeout
+        while not await self.registry.try_reclaim(slot.version):
+            if time.monotonic() > deadline:
+                raise TimeoutError(f"Version {slot.version} still leased after {self.reclaim_timeout}s")
+            await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
+        slot.version = None
+        return slot
+
+    @torch.no_grad()
+    async def publish(
+        self, weights: Iterator[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]] | AsyncIterator[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]], version: int
+    ) -> WeightManifest:
+        """Copy `weights` into a free slot and announce them as `version`.
+
+        The tensor names, shapes and dtypes must be the same, in the same order, on every call.
+        """
+        start = time.time()

+            # first version to size the slots.
+            named = [

+                async for n, t in ensure_async_iterator(weights)
+            ]
+            self._setup(named)
+            weights = iter(named)
+
+        slot = await self._acquire_slot()

+        async for name, tensor in ensure_async_iterator(weights):

+            if (name, tensor.shape, self._wire_dtype(tensor.dtype)) != (spec.name, spec.shape, spec.dtype):

When periodic or final validation is enabled, `PPOTrainer.fit()` calls `_validate()` immediately after this hook, but `_publish_weights()` only reads agent states without waiting for the published version to load. In `decoupled_async`, these standalone replicas allocate GPUs outside the trainer's resource-pool manager, but the new trainer inherits `PPOTrainer._get_n_gpus_for_throughput()`, which counts only that manager's GPUs. The corresponding override remains exclusively in `PPOTrainerSeparateAsync` rather than the shared mixin. A 4-training/4-rollout run is consequently normalized by 4 instead of 8 and reports twice its actual per-GPU `perf/throughput`, invalidating comparisons between the modes. Share or implement the standalone-aware GPU counter.

detail.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds `decoupled_async`, a v1 trainer mode in which the trainer never drives rollout. The trainer only publishes weight versions and enqueues prompts in TransferQueue. Each vLLM replica pulls new versions with one-sided reads and decides on its own when to load them, and a rollout-side dispatcher starts enqueued prompts once replicas have the weights they require.

In `separate_async` today, every step ends with `CheckpointEngineManager.update_weights`: abort all requests, release KV, build a topology, push weights, resume. The trainer waits for it and every replica pauses at once. In `decoupled_async` the trainer's per-step weight work is a copy into a host slot; replicas prefetch while generating and pause only to load (~1 s at 0.5B, ~1.5 s at 8B).

Design doc: `docs/advance/decoupled_weight_sync.md`.

**Related work and why this is not a duplicate.** #8395 (`sharded_nixl`) moves only each rollout rank's TP/EP slice with NIXL writes, but stays trainer-pushed inside `CheckpointEngineManager`. #7108 is Megatron→SGLang P2P over Mooncake, also trainer-driven. #8168 adds standalone replica lifecycle APIs. This PR changes who drives the sync (rollout pulls on its own schedule) and removes the trainer's calls into rollout; it transfers full tensors. #8395's slice planning is the natural next step for sharded pulls on top of this.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: [decoupled weight sync](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+decoupled+weight+sync), [transport_pull](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+transport_pull), [prompt dispatcher](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+prompt+dispatcher), [torch.distributed._transport](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+torch.distributed._transport)
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

### Test

Hardware: one node, 8× H100 80GB SXM (NVLink, no InfiniBand), `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0` (NVLS multicast is unavailable on that VM). verl's locked env (torch 2.13, vLLM 0.32) unless noted.

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/trainer/ppo/v1/ tests/checkpoint_engine/test_weight_update_agent_on_cpu.py tests/checkpoint_engine/test_transport_pull_on_cpu.py tests/checkpoint_engine/test_transport_registry_on_cpu.py` (includes the new prompt dispatcher, decoupled_async and replay-buffer tests) | 269 passed |
| `pytest tests/checkpoint_engine/test_transport_pull_on_gpu.py` (torch 2.15 + nixl 1.5.2, both `nixl` and `nixl_native`) | 4 passed |
| `pytest tests/checkpoint_engine/test_correctness_on_gpu.py -k transport_pull` (FSDP Qwen3-8B → 6 mock rollout workers, 3 syncs, weights checked; torch 2.15) | passed for both transports |
| `pytest tests/utils/test_bucketed_weight_transfer.py -k IPC` | 8 passed |
| `pytest tests/workers/rollout/rollout_vllm/test_vllm_weight_update_agent.py` (real vLLM replica, versions 0→1→2 under load) | 1 passed |

End-to-end async GRPO on GSM8K (`tests/special_e2e/run_v1_separate_async.sh`, 4 train + 4 rollout GPUs, one seed), `separate_async` + `nccl` against `decoupled_async`:

| | `separate_async` + `nccl` | `decoupled_async` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, 30 steps: validation accuracy at steps 10 / 20 / 30 | 0.079 / 0.438 / 0.477 | 0.327 / 0.456 / 0.501 |
| 0.5B: step time / trainer time in `update_weights` | 5.80 s / 1.26 s | 4.74 s / 0.14 s |
| Qwen3-8B-Base, 20 steps, `bypass_mode=True`: validation accuracy at steps 0 / 10 / 20 | 0.638 / 0.870 / 0.896 | 0.644 / 0.860 / 0.887 |
| 8B: step time / trainer waiting for samples | 4.78 s / 0.05 s | 6.08 s / 2.47 s |
| `off_policy/trajectory_spans/mean` (both sizes) | 1.0 | 1.0 |

Accuracy matches within single-seed noise, and every trajectory is generated by a single weight version. Before the prompt dispatcher existed (weights pulled, prompts pushed by the trainer), 1.8–2.0 versions per trajectory were typical because prompts dispatched right after a publish were aborted and re-prefilled. Performance is not optimized yet: at 8B a replica update (full-copy pulls through host memory, ~6.3 s) is longer than a training step, so prompts wait for it; the NCCL baseline moves the 16 GB in 1.35 s. `min_version_lag=2` does not help (5.60 s per step), and admitting prompts on older weights would only get them aborted by the next update. Sharded pulls are the fix and are left for a follow-up; the goal here is separating rollout from the training loop.

### API and Usage Example

```bash
bash tests/special_e2e/run_v1_separate_async.sh \
    trainer.v1.trainer_mode=decoupled_async \
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.checkpoint_engine.backend=transport_pull \
    algorithm.rollout_correction.bypass_mode=True
```

New config (all additive): `trainer.v1.decoupled_async.{num_warmup_batches, parameter_sync_step, min_version_lag, poll_interval, init_timeout, max_inflight_prompts, dispatch_poll_interval}` and `checkpoint_engine.engine_kwargs.transport_pull.{device, transport, num_slots, rollout_dtype, lease_ttl, registry_name}`. The `transport_pull` backend also works under the existing `CheckpointEngineManager` flow.

### Design & Code Changes

Weight transfer, `verl/checkpoint_engine/transport/`:

- `registry.py`: directory of published versions (READY → RETIRED → reclaimed) with TTL reader leases judged on the registry's clock; a named Ray actor scoped to the job.
- `publisher.py`: the last `num_slots` versions live in pinned host buffers registered once; a slot is overwritten only after every lease on its version ends. fp32 weights are cast to `rollout_dtype` (bf16) on the way in.
- `puller.py`: leases a version, reads all buckets into a local registered mirror, and rejects the copy if the lease lapsed mid-read.
- `nixl_native.py`, `transport.py`: transports. `nixl_native` uses NIXL's bindings and runs on any torch; other names go to `torch.distributed._transport` (torch >= 2.15, which released vLLM does not support yet).
- `engine.py`: the `transport_pull` checkpoint engine (`send_weights` publishes, `prefetch`, `receive_weights`).
- `update_agent.py`: `WeightUpdateAgent`, one per vLLM replica. It prefetches a newer version while generating, then aborts in-flight requests, releases KV, loads the mirror, restores KV and resumes.

Trainer, `verl/trainer/ppo/v1/`:

- `trainer_decoupled_async.py`: publishes at init and step end, enqueues prompts with a `min_weight_version` tag, and on resume only resets interrupted prompts to `pending`. Before validation, which bypasses the dispatcher, it waits for every replica to serve the newest version. It makes no calls that control rollout (24 in `separate_async`).
- `prompt_dispatcher.py`: one per rollout service; claims pending prompts oldest first, up to `max_inflight_prompts`, once every replica has their version, and starts them on the agent loop workers.
- `standalone_rollout.py`: `StandaloneRolloutMixin` with what `separate_async` and `decoupled_async` share (standalone replicas, `DetachActorWorker`, Decoupled PPO old log-probs), moved verbatim out of `separate_async`.
- `replay_buffer.py`: in `decoupled_async`, a group's age for off-policy control (eviction, its metrics, and `sample()`'s assertion) is measured from the oldest weight version its trajectories started on; other modes keep the enqueue step. An optional `health_check_fn` runs on every poll so a failed agent or dispatcher fails the job instead of leaving `sample()` waiting.

Other fixes found along the way:

- `bucketed_weight_transfer.py`: weights larger than the bucket that arrive in host memory are staged on the GPU before CUDA IPC (`reduce_tensor` on a CPU tensor yields a shared-memory handle that `rebuild_ipc` cannot rebuild). Hit by Qwen3-8B's 1.24 GB embedding. The staged copy is returned to the device after the receiver acks. This also affects `nixl` with `device=cpu`.
- `CheckpointEngineWorker.prefetch_weights` for engines that support prefetching.

Review findings addressed since the first revision: the missing `on_sample_end` hook; pinned host buffers on CPU-only machines; fencing device-to-host copies before a version is announced; releasing the lease when a read fails; one staleness clock across eviction and `sample()`; syncing replicas before validation; the update agent loading the first version regardless of `min_version_lag`; counting rollout GPUs in throughput; the `separate_async` config comment.

Follow-ups (see the design doc): `keep` pause mode, version-aware routing, sharded pulls, a run epoch for resume once the registry outlives the job, reclaiming prompts from dead agent loop workers.

+# Decoupled Async Trainer: Rollout Pulls Weights and Prompts
+
+**Authors:** Luosuu
+
+**Last updated:** 2026-11-03
+
+## Background
+
+In the v1 `separate_async` trainer, the trainer drives rollout. At the end of every step,
+`CheckpointEngineManager.update_weights` aborts in-flight requests on every rollout replica, releases
+their KV cache, builds a transfer topology, pushes the weights, and resumes generation. The trainer
+waits for all of it, and every replica pauses at the same moment. Prompts are pushed to the agent loop
+workers by the trainer as well.
+
+The `decoupled_async` trainer mode turns this around. The trainer only **publishes** weight versions
+and **enqueues** prompts in TransferQueue. Each rollout replica **pulls** new versions with one-sided
+reads and decides on its own when to load them, and a rollout-side dispatcher starts enqueued prompts.
+The trainer never pauses, aborts or waits for rollout.
+
+## Architecture
+
+```
+trainer rank 0 --copy--> WeightPublisher (versioned host slots, registered once)
+                              | publish(v): manifest {version, layout, descriptors, endpoint}
+                              v
+                       WeightRegistry  <-- latest_ready / lease --  WeightUpdateAgent (per replica)
+                                                                        | prefetch, then apply
+                                                                        v
+                     CheckpointEngineWorker (transport_pull) -- one-sided READ --> host mirror --> vLLM
+
+trainer --enqueue pending prompts (min_weight_version)--> TransferQueue
+                                                              ^
+                       PromptDispatcher -- claim when every replica has the version --> agent loop workers
+```
+
+| Component | Role |
+| --- | --- |
+| `checkpoint_engine/transport/registry.py` | Directory of published versions (`READY` → `RETIRED` → reclaimed) and reader leases. Leases expire on the registry's clock, so a crashed reader cannot pin a version. `RayWeightRegistry` runs it as a named Ray actor scoped to the job. |
+| `checkpoint_engine/transport/publisher.py` | Keeps the last `num_slots` versions in pinned host buffers that are registered once. A slot is overwritten only after every lease on its version ends. fp32 weights are cast to `rollout_dtype` (bf16 by default) on the way in. |
+| `checkpoint_engine/transport/puller.py` | Leases a version, reads every bucket into a local registered mirror, and rejects the copy if the lease lapsed mid-read (torn read). |
+| `checkpoint_engine/transport/transport.py`, `nixl_native.py` | Slot layout and transports. `nixl_native` uses NIXL's own bindings and runs on any torch. Other names go to `torch.distributed._transport` (torch >= 2.15). Trainer and rollout must use the same transport. |
+| `checkpoint_engine/transport/engine.py` | The `transport_pull` checkpoint engine. `send_weights` publishes, `prefetch` pulls ahead of time, `receive_weights` hands the pulled version to the inference engine. It also works under the classic `CheckpointEngineManager` flow. |
+| `checkpoint_engine/transport/update_agent.py` | `WeightUpdateAgent`: one per vLLM replica; decides when the replica updates. |
+| `trainer/ppo/v1/prompt_dispatcher.py` | `PromptDispatcher`: claims enqueued prompts and starts them on the agent loop workers. |
+| `trainer/ppo/v1/trainer_decoupled_async.py` | `PPOTrainerDecoupledAsync`: publishes, enqueues, samples and trains. |
+
+## When a replica updates
+
+Each update has two phases, and only the second pauses generation:
+
+1. **Prefetch.** Once the newest READY version is at least `min_version_lag` ahead of the loaded one,
+   every checkpoint engine worker of the replica pulls it into its host mirror while vLLM keeps
+   generating.
+2. **Apply.** Abort in-flight requests, release the KV cache, load the mirror, restore the KV cache
+   and resume. `FullyAsyncLLMServerClient` resubmits aborted requests with their partial output, so
+   they are re-prefilled under the new weights. A failure during apply leaves the replica paused
+   rather than serving mixed weights, and the trainer fails the job.
+
+`min_version_lag` must stay below `trainer.v1.sampler.max_off_policy_threshold`. Otherwise rollout
+produces samples the trainer drops.
+
+## Prompt dispatch
+
+The trainer enqueues prompts exactly where it used to dispatch them (warmup, once per step, and the
+replay buffer's refills), but only writes them to TransferQueue as `pending`. Each prompt carries a
+`min_weight_version`: the newest published version, minus `min_version_lag - 1`.
+
+One `PromptDispatcher` per rollout service polls TransferQueue and claims pending prompts, oldest first
+and up to `max_inflight_prompts`, once every replica has loaded their `min_weight_version`. Prompts
+enqueued right after a publish therefore wait for the update instead of starting on the old weights and
+being re-prefilled. There is a single dispatcher because TransferQueue tags are last-writer-wins, so
+independent claimers could start the same prompt twice. On resume, the trainer only resets interrupted
+prompts to `pending`; the dispatcher starts them again.
+
+## Staleness
+
+The step at which a prompt was enqueued no longer tells which weights generated it. The replay buffer
+therefore measures a group's lag from the oldest weight version any of its trajectories started on
+(`min_global_steps`, already recorded per trajectory). Version `v` is published at the end of step `v`,
+so a group generated entirely by the newest weights has lag 1, the same as a freshly dispatched group
+under the default clock.
+
+## Usage
+
+```bash
+bash tests/special_e2e/run_v1_separate_async.sh \
+    trainer.v1.trainer_mode=decoupled_async \
+    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.checkpoint_engine.backend=transport_pull \
+    algorithm.rollout_correction.bypass_mode=True
+```
+
+`bypass_mode=True` uses rollout's log-probs as the old policy. Without it, and with
+`parameter_sync_step > 1`, the trainer saves and restores the full model on CPU for every later
+mini-batch to recompute them, which dominates the step for large models.
+
+| Option | Default | Meaning |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `trainer.v1.decoupled_async.num_warmup_batches` | `1` | Batches enqueued before the training loop starts. |
+| `trainer.v1.decoupled_async.parameter_sync_step` | `4` | Local updates per published weight version. |
+| `trainer.v1.decoupled_async.min_version_lag` | `1` | Versions a replica may fall behind before it updates. Keep `1`: prompts are admitted only on the newest weights, so a lazier replica makes them wait for its whole update. |
+| `trainer.v1.decoupled_async.poll_interval` | `0.5` | Seconds between registry polls per replica. |
+| `trainer.v1.decoupled_async.init_timeout` | `600` | Seconds the trainer waits at startup for every replica to load the initial weights. |
+| `trainer.v1.decoupled_async.max_inflight_prompts` | `null` | Prompt groups generating at once across all replicas; `null` for no limit. |
+| `trainer.v1.decoupled_async.dispatch_poll_interval` | `0.2` | Seconds between TransferQueue polls of the dispatcher. |
+| `checkpoint_engine.engine_kwargs.transport_pull.device` | `cpu` | Slot and mirror memory. Each slot holds a full model copy, which rarely fits on a trainer GPU. |
+| `checkpoint_engine.engine_kwargs.transport_pull.transport` | `nixl_native` | `nixl_native`, or a `torch.distributed._transport` backend such as `nixl`. |
+| `checkpoint_engine.engine_kwargs.transport_pull.num_slots` | `2` | Versions the publisher keeps at once. |
+| `checkpoint_engine.engine_kwargs.transport_pull.rollout_dtype` | `bfloat16` | dtype fp32 weights are cast to before publishing; `null` disables the cast. |
+
+## Results
+
+### What is decoupled
+
+| | `separate_async` | `decoupled_async` |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Trainer calls that control rollout (abort, sleep, KV release/resume, weight push, load balancer add/remove, mode switch, `generate_sequences`) | 24 | 0 |
+| Trainer mode size | 371 lines, plus hybrid switching state | 221 lines; shared standalone pieces in a 108-line mixin |
+| What the trainer knows about rollout | Replica handles, load balancer, pause/resume protocol, KV memory lifecycle | Publish a version, enqueue prompts, sample from TransferQueue |
+
+`decoupled_async` still starts the update agents and the dispatcher, because rollout runs in the same
+Ray job, but after that it only checks their health.
+
+### Correctness
+
+All runs: GSM8K async GRPO, 4 training + 4 rollout H100s on one node, `parameter_sync_step=4`,
+32 prompts × 4 responses per step, one seed.
+
+| Run | Validation accuracy, baseline | Validation accuracy, `decoupled_async` | Weight versions per trajectory |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, 30 steps, `bypass_mode=False` (steps 10 / 20 / 30) | 0.079 / 0.438 / 0.477 | 0.327 / 0.456 / 0.501 | 1.0 |
+| Qwen3-8B-Base, 20 steps, `bypass_mode=True` (steps 0 / 10 / 20) | 0.638 / 0.870 / 0.896 | 0.644 / 0.860 / 0.887 | 1.0 |
+
+Accuracy matches the `separate_async` + `nccl` baseline within single-seed noise, and every trajectory
+is generated by a single weight version. Before the prompt dispatcher existed (weights pulled, prompts
+still pushed by the trainer), 1.8–2.0 versions per trajectory were typical: prompts dispatched right
+after a publish started on the old weights and were re-prefilled when the replica updated.
+
+### Performance (not yet optimized)
+
+| | Baseline | `decoupled_async` |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| 0.5B: step time / trainer time in `update_weights` | 5.80 s / 1.26 s | 4.74 s / 0.14 s |
+| 0.5B: replica prefetch / pause | — | 0.33 s / ≤ 0.93 s |
+| 8B: step time / trainer time in `update_weights` | 4.78 s / 1.35 s | 6.08 s / 0.23 s |
+| 8B: trainer waiting for samples (`timing_s/gen`) | 0.05 s | 2.47 s |
+| 8B: replica prefetch / pause | — | 4.8 s / 1.5 s |
+
+At 0.5B a replica update (~1.3 s) is much shorter than a step and decoupling saves the trainer's sync
+time. At 8B it is slower: a replica update (~6.3 s) takes longer than a training step (~4.8 s), and
+because the dispatcher admits prompts only once every replica has the newest version, new prompts wait
+and the trainer runs short of samples. The baseline's NCCL broadcast moves the 16 GB in 1.35 s, while
+each rollout rank here pulls the full model from one publisher through host memory. With
+`min_version_lag=2` the replicas update only every other version, so the waits alternate between none
+and a whole update (5.60 s per step); the dispatcher should keep admitting on the newest weights,
+otherwise admitted prompts are aborted by the next update anyway. The fix is a faster transfer (sharded
+pulls, GPU-direct publishing), not looser gating.
+
+## Next: rollout outside the trainer's Ray job
+
+`decoupled_async` removes the trainer's calls into rollout, but everything still runs in one Ray job: the
+trainer launches the vLLM replicas, checkpoint engine workers, agent loop workers, update agents and
+the dispatcher, and both sides find the weight registry and TransferQueue as named Ray actors. The next
+step is a rollout service with its own lifecycle, possibly its own Ray cluster, that meets the trainer
+only at the weight registry and TransferQueue.
+
+What already works across that boundary:
+
+- **Weight transfer.** One-sided reads need only the endpoint URL and serialized descriptors in the
+  manifest; NIXL/UCX does not depend on Ray. Trainer and rollout nodes must be reachable over the
+  network (RDMA or TCP).
+- **TransferQueue data path.** In TransferQueue 0.1.11 a client (`TransferQueueClient` plus its storage
+  manager) only *connects* ZMQ DEALER sockets to the controller and storage units, using addresses in
+  the TransferQueue config (`controller.zmq_info`, `backend.SimpleStorage.zmq_info`). The
+  `SimpleStorage` and `MooncakeStore` backends are reachable without Ray; the `RayStorage` backend is
+  not.
+- **Control.** The trainer never calls rollout; it only publishes weights and enqueues prompts.
+
+What is missing:
+
+| Gap | Today | Needed |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Weight registry | Named Ray actor (`RayWeightRegistry`) | An etcd or Redis implementation of `WeightRegistry`; leases already expire on the registry's clock |
+| TransferQueue discovery | `tq.init()` finds the controller with `ray.get_actor("TransferQueueController")` and reads its config | Publish the TransferQueue config (controller and storage ZMQ addresses) through the registry store, and a public connect-from-config API in TransferQueue; today `interface._maybe_create_tq_client(conf)` does this but is private |
+| TransferQueue outside Ray | `ray.get_runtime_context()` in the storage manager's thread pool sizing starts a local Ray instance in a process without Ray | Guard it with `ray.is_initialized()` (TransferQueue change) |
+| Rollout launcher | The trainer creates replicas, agents, agent loop workers and the dispatcher | A rollout-service entry point that creates them, with reward workers if rewards are computed in the agent loop |
+| Version identity | Versions are trainer steps; the registry dies with the job | A run epoch in each version, so a resumed trainer can republish older weights to a registry that outlived it |
+| Lifecycle | TransferQueue's controller and storage live in the trainer's Ray job | The rollout service tolerates trainer restarts (reconnect), or TransferQueue runs as its own service |
+| Security | ZMQ and NIXL endpoints are unauthenticated | Network isolation between the two clusters, or authenticated transports |
+
+Inside the rollout service, Ray remains a convenient way to place each vLLM server and its checkpoint
+engine worker on the same GPU and to call between agent, server and worker; it would simply be the
+service's own cluster, sized independently of training.
+
+### Reusing an existing vLLM deployment
+
+Today each replica is launched by verl: a `vLLMHttpServer` Ray actor with verl's worker extension, and a
+checkpoint engine worker per GPU that hands pulled weights to vLLM over CUDA IPC. vLLM 0.32 already has
+what a standard `vllm serve` deployment would need instead:
+
+- HTTP RL endpoints: `/pause`, `/resume`, `/abort_requests`, `/init_weight_transfer_engine`,
+  `/start_weight_update`, `/update_weights`, `/finish_weight_update`, `/update_weight_version`.
+- Pluggable weight transfer (`WeightTransferEngineFactory.register_engine`, selected at startup with
+  `weight_transfer_config`), which verl already uses for delta sync.
+- Per-token weight version spans in request outputs.
+
+With a pull engine running inside the vLLM workers (registered as a plugin; also where sharded pulls
+belong), an HTTP update agent, and agent loops calling vLLM over HTTP, rollout becomes a standard vLLM
+deployment plus a pip-installed plugin, and `/pause`'s `keep` mode comes for free. The engine is chosen
+at startup, so the deployment must be launched with the plugin; it cannot be attached to a vLLM that
+is already running without it.
+
+## Limitations and follow-ups
+
+- **Weight transfer speed.** Full copies through host memory are slower than the NCCL path at 8B; see
+  Performance.
+- **`keep` pause mode** to resume long in-flight requests on their old-weight KV cache instead of
+  re-prefilling them.
+- **Version-aware routing.** The dispatcher waits until every replica has a prompt's version; routing
+  to any replica that is already new enough would start prompts sooner.
+- **Full copies.** Every rollout rank pulls the whole model from trainer rank 0. Sharded pulls (each
+  rank reads only its TP/EP slice from each trainer rank) and P2P relays come next.
+- **Checkpoint resume** needs a run epoch in the version once the registry outlives the job, so a
+  resumed trainer can republish older weights.
+- **Agent loop worker failures.** Prompts claimed by a worker that dies stay `running`; the dispatcher
+  does not reclaim them yet.

+"""Publisher/puller logic against an in-process fake of torch.distributed._transport."""
+
+import asyncio
+import pickle
+import uuid
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from verl.checkpoint_engine.transport import InMemoryWeightRegistry
+from verl.checkpoint_engine.transport.engine import TransportPullCheckpointEngine
+from verl.checkpoint_engine.transport.publisher import WeightPublisher
+from verl.checkpoint_engine.transport.puller import TornReadError, WeightPuller
+from verl.checkpoint_engine.transport.transport import TENSOR_ALIGNMENT
+
+_ENDPOINTS: dict[bytes, "_FakeTransport"] = {}
+
+
+class _FakeRemoteBuffer:
+    def __init__(self, url, key, size):
+        self.url, self.key, self.size = url, key, size
+
+    def serialize(self) -> bytes:
+        return pickle.dumps((self.url, self.key, self.size))
+
+    @classmethod
+    def deserialize(cls, data: bytes):
+        return cls(*pickle.loads(data))
+
+
+class _FakeMemory:
+    def __init__(self, transport, tensor):
+        self.transport, self.tensor, self.key = transport, tensor, uuid.uuid4().hex
+
+    def to_remote_buffer(self):
+        return _FakeRemoteBuffer(self.transport.url, self.key, self.tensor.numel())
+
+    def to_mutable_view(self):
+        return self.tensor
+
+
+class _FakeTransport:
+    """One-sided reads copy straight out of the peer's registered tensors."""
+
+    def __init__(self, backend, device):
+        self.url, self.peer, self.memories = None, None, {}
+        self.before_read = None
+
+    def bind(self):
+        self.url = uuid.uuid4().hex.encode()
+        _ENDPOINTS[self.url] = self
+        return self.url
+
+    def connect(self, url):
+        self.peer = url
+
+    def register_memory(self, tensor):
+        memory = _FakeMemory(self, tensor)
+        self.memories[memory.key] = memory
+        return memory
+
+    def unregister_memory(self, memory):
+        del self.memories[memory.key]
+
+    async def read_async(self, local, remote):
+        assert remote.url == self.peer, "read from an endpoint that was not connected"
+        source = _ENDPOINTS[remote.url].memories[remote.key].tensor
+        assert local.numel() == source.numel() == remote.size
+        if self.before_read is not None:
+            self.before_read()
+        local.copy_(source)
+
+    def close(self):
+        _ENDPOINTS.pop(self.url, None)
+
+
+class _FakeClock:
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.now = 0.0
+
+    def __call__(self):
+        return self.now
+
+
+def _weights(step: int):
+    # A 2-D fp32 tensor larger than one bucket, an odd-sized bf16 one to exercise alignment, an int one.
+    return [
+        ("big.weight", torch.arange(3000, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(30, 100) + step),
+        ("odd.bias", torch.full((7,), float(step), dtype=torch.bfloat16)),
+        ("ids", torch.arange(5, dtype=torch.int64) * step),
+    ]
+
+
+def _publisher(registry, **kwargs):
+    kwargs.setdefault("rollout_dtype", None)
+    return WeightPublisher(registry, bucket_size=4096, device="cpu", transport_factory=_FakeTransport, **kwargs)
+
+
+def _on_wire(tensor, rollout_dtype=torch.bfloat16):
+    return tensor.to(rollout_dtype) if tensor.dtype == torch.float32 else tensor
+
+
+def _puller(registry, **kwargs):
+    return WeightPuller(registry, device="cpu", transport_factory=_FakeTransport, poll_interval=0.01, **kwargs)
+
+
+def _run(coro):
+    return asyncio.run(coro)
+
+
+def test_publish_then_pull_is_bit_exact():
+    async def main():
+        registry = InMemoryWeightRegistry()
+        publisher, puller = _publisher(registry), _puller(registry)
+
+        manifest = await publisher.publish(iter(_weights(1)), version=1)
+        assert len(manifest.buckets) > 1, "the big tensor should span several buckets"
+        assert all(spec.offset % TENSOR_ALIGNMENT == 0 for spec in manifest.tensors)
+
+        pulled = await puller.fetch(await puller.wait_for_version(1, timeout=1))
+        received = dict(pulled.named_tensors())
+        for name, expected in _weights(1):
+            assert received[name].dtype == expected.dtype and torch.equal(received[name], expected), name
+
+        # A lease is held only during the fetch.
+        assert not registry._leases
+
+    _run(main())

+def test_fp32_weights_are_cast_to_rollout_dtype():
+    async def main():
+        registry = InMemoryWeightRegistry()
+        publisher, puller = _publisher(registry, rollout_dtype=torch.bfloat16), _puller(registry)
+        for step in (1, 2):
+            manifest = await publisher.publish(iter(_weights(step)), version=step)
+            received = dict((await puller.fetch(manifest)).named_tensors())
+            for name, expected in _weights(step):
+                assert received[name].dtype == _on_wire(expected).dtype, name
+                assert torch.equal(received[name], _on_wire(expected)), name
+        # The fp32 tensor takes half the bytes; bf16 and int64 tensors are unchanged.
+        assert {spec.name: spec.dtype for spec in manifest.tensors} == {
+            "big.weight": torch.bfloat16,
+            "odd.bias": torch.bfloat16,
+            "ids": torch.int64,
+        }
+
+    _run(main())

+def test_registrations_are_reused_across_versions():
+    async def main():
+        registry = InMemoryWeightRegistry()
+        publisher, puller = _publisher(registry), _puller(registry)
+        await publisher.publish(iter(_weights(1)), version=1)
+        await puller.fetch(await registry.latest_ready())
+        publisher_memories = [id(m) for slot in publisher.slots for m in slot.memories]
+        puller_memories = [id(m) for m in puller.memories]
+
+        for step in (2, 3, 4):
+            await publisher.publish(iter(_weights(step)), version=step)
+            pulled = await puller.fetch(await registry.latest_ready())
+            assert pulled.version == step
+            assert torch.equal(dict(pulled.named_tensors())["big.weight"], _weights(step)[0][1])
+
+        assert [id(m) for slot in publisher.slots for m in slot.memories] == publisher_memories
+        assert [id(m) for m in puller.memories] == puller_memories
+        # Two slots: only the newest version is READY, older ones are gone once unleased.
+        assert sorted(registry._states) == [3, 4]
+        assert (await registry.latest_ready()).version == 4
+
+    _run(main())

+def test_publisher_waits_for_reader_lease_before_overwriting():
+    async def main():
+        registry = InMemoryWeightRegistry()
+        publisher = _publisher(registry, reclaim_timeout=0.2)
+        await publisher.publish(iter(_weights(1)), version=1)
+        await publisher.publish(iter(_weights(2)), version=2)
+
+        # A slow reader still holds version 1, whose slot is next to be overwritten.
+        lease = await registry.acquire_lease(2, ttl=60)
+        registry._leases[lease.lease_id].version = 1
+        with pytest.raises(TimeoutError):
+            await publisher.publish(iter(_weights(3)), version=3)
+
+        await registry.release_lease(lease.lease_id)
+        await publisher.publish(iter(_weights(3)), version=3)
+        assert (await registry.latest_ready()).version == 3
+
+    _run(main())

+def test_torn_read_is_rejected():
+    async def main():
+        clock = _FakeClock()
+        registry = InMemoryWeightRegistry(clock=clock)
+        publisher, puller = _publisher(registry), _puller(registry, lease_ttl=60)
+        manifest = await publisher.publish(iter(_weights(1)), version=1)
+
+        puller._setup(manifest)
+
+        def stall():
+            # The read outlives the lease, as if the reader was descheduled without renewing.
+            clock.now += 120
+
+        puller.transport.before_read = stall
+        with pytest.raises(TornReadError):
+            await puller.fetch(manifest)
+
+    _run(main())

+def test_layout_change_is_rejected():

+        registry = InMemoryWeightRegistry()
+        publisher = _publisher(registry)
+        await publisher.publish(iter(_weights(1)), version=1)
+        weights = _weights(2)
+        weights[1] = ("odd.bias", torch.zeros(8, dtype=torch.bfloat16))
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="does not match layout"):
+            await publisher.publish(iter(weights), version=2)
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Got 2 weights"):
+            await publisher.publish(iter(_weights(2)[:2]), version=2)

+def test_checkpoint_engine_round_trip():
+    async def main():
+        registry = InMemoryWeightRegistry()
+
+        def engine(is_master):
+            e = TransportPullCheckpointEngine(
+                bucket_size=4096, device="cpu", is_master=is_master, transport_factory=_FakeTransport
+            )
+            e._registry = registry
+            return e
+
+        trainer, other_rank, rollout = engine(True), engine(False), engine(False)
+        assert TransportPullCheckpointEngine.build_topology(2, 3, [{}] * 5) == ({}, {})
+
+        async def receive(step):
+            return {n: t.clone() async for n, t in rollout.receive_weights(global_steps=step)}
+
+        for step in (1, 2):
+            # As in CheckpointEngineManager, both sides run concurrently; the rollout waits for the version.
+            received, _, _ = await asyncio.gather(
+                receive(step),
+                trainer.send_weights(iter(_weights(step)), global_steps=step),
+                other_rank.send_weights(iter(_weights(step)), global_steps=step),
+            )
+            for name, expected in _weights(step):
+                assert torch.equal(received[name], _on_wire(expected)), name
+        assert other_rank.publisher is None
+
+        # Re-syncing an already published step drains the weights without publishing again.
+        drained = []
+        await trainer.send_weights((drained.append(n) or (n, t) for n, t in _weights(9)), global_steps=2)
+        assert len(drained) == 3 and (await registry.latest_ready()).version == 2
+
+        # Without global_steps, each sync is one version past the previous one on both sides.
+        for step in (3, 4):
+            received, _ = await asyncio.gather(receive(None), trainer.send_weights(iter(_weights(step))))
+            assert torch.equal(received["ids"], _weights(step)[2][1])
+        assert trainer.last_version == rollout.last_version == 4
+
+    _run(main())

+"""Publisher and pullers on separate GPUs, reading over a real transport. No model needed."""
+
+import importlib.util
+
+import pytest
+import ray
+import torch
+
+from verl.checkpoint_engine.transport import RayWeightRegistry
+from verl.checkpoint_engine.transport.publisher import WeightPublisher
+from verl.checkpoint_engine.transport.puller import WeightPuller
+from verl.utils.device import get_torch_device
+
+_NUM_PULLERS = 3
+
+
+def _backend_available(backend: str) -> bool:
+    if backend == "nixl_native":
+        return importlib.util.find_spec("nixl") is not None
+    return importlib.util.find_spec("torch.distributed._transport") is not None
+
+
+def _weights(version: int, device: str):
+    # Deterministic from the version, so readers can rebuild the expected values themselves.
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(version)
+    shapes = [
+        ((4096, 4096), torch.bfloat16),
+        ((11008, 4096), torch.bfloat16),
+        ((4097,), torch.float32),
+        ((3,), torch.int64),
+    ]
+    out = []
+    for i, (shape, dtype) in enumerate(shapes):
+        values = (
+            torch.randint(0, 1000, shape, generator=gen) if dtype == torch.int64 else torch.randn(shape, generator=gen)
+        )
+        out.append((f"layer{i}", values.to(dtype).to(device)))
+    return out
+
+
+@ray.remote(num_gpus=1)
+class _Publisher:
+    def __init__(self, backend, device):
+        self.publisher = WeightPublisher(
+            RayWeightRegistry(name="test_transport_pull"), bucket_size=64 << 20, device=device, backend=backend
+        )
+
+    async def publish(self, version):
+        await self.publisher.publish(iter(_weights(version, "cuda")), version=version)
+
+
+@ray.remote(num_gpus=1)
+class _Puller:
+    def __init__(self, backend, device):
+        self.puller = WeightPuller(RayWeightRegistry(name="test_transport_pull"), device=device, backend=backend)
+
+    async def pull(self, min_version):
+        manifest = await self.puller.wait_for_version(min_version, timeout=120)
+        pulled = await self.puller.fetch(manifest)
+        received = dict(pulled.named_tensors())
+        # The publisher casts fp32 weights to its rollout_dtype, bf16 by default.
+        expected = [
+            (n, t.to(torch.bfloat16) if t.dtype == torch.float32 else t) for n, t in _weights(pulled.version, "cpu")
+        ]
+        mismatched = [name for name, tensor in expected if not torch.equal(received[name].cpu(), tensor)]
+        get_torch_device().synchronize()
+        return pulled.version, mismatched
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("device", ["cuda", "cpu"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("backend", ["nixl", "nixl_native"])
+def test_publish_and_pull_across_gpus(backend, device):
+    if not _backend_available(backend):
+        pytest.skip(f"{backend} is not installed")
+    if get_torch_device().device_count() < 1 + _NUM_PULLERS:
+        pytest.skip(f"needs {1 + _NUM_PULLERS} GPUs")
+
+    ray.init(namespace=f"test_transport_pull_{backend}_{device}")
+    try:
+        publisher = _Publisher.remote(backend, device)
+        pullers = [_Puller.remote(backend, device) for _ in range(_NUM_PULLERS)]
+        for version in range(1, 4):
+            # Pullers wait on the registry while the publisher writes, as rollout replicas would.
+            pulls = [p.pull.remote(version) for p in pullers]
+            ray.get(publisher.publish.remote(version))
+            for got_version, mismatched in ray.get(pulls):
+                assert got_version == version
+                assert not mismatched, f"version {version}: {mismatched}"
+    finally:
+        ray.shutdown()

+        assert not await registry.try_reclaim(1)
+        await registry.retire(1)
+        with pytest.raises(LeaseError):
+            await registry.acquire_lease(1, ttl=10)
+        assert not await registry.try_reclaim(1)
+
+        await registry.release_lease(lease.lease_id)
+        assert await registry.try_reclaim(1)

+def test_lease_expiry_reclaims_crashed_reader():
+    async def main():
+        clock = _FakeClock()
+        registry = InMemoryWeightRegistry(clock=clock)
+        await registry.publish(_manifest(1))
+        lease = await registry.acquire_lease(1, ttl=10)
+        await registry.retire(1)
+
+        # Renewal during a long read keeps the version pinned past the original ttl.
+        clock.now = 8
+        await registry.renew_lease(lease.lease_id, ttl=10)
+        clock.now = 15
+        assert await registry.is_lease_valid(lease.lease_id)
+        assert not await registry.try_reclaim(1)
+
+        # The reader stops renewing, e.g. it crashed: the lease expires on the registry's clock.
+        clock.now = 18
+        assert not await registry.is_lease_valid(lease.lease_id)
+        with pytest.raises(LeaseError):
+            await registry.renew_lease(lease.lease_id, ttl=10)
+        assert await registry.try_reclaim(1)
+
+    _run(main())

+def test_fencing_detects_expired_lease_after_read():
+    async def main():
+        clock = _FakeClock()
+        registry = InMemoryWeightRegistry(clock=clock)
+        await registry.publish(_manifest(1))

+        clock.now = 6
+        assert await registry.try_reclaim(1)

+def test_ray_registry_shared_by_name():

+class _Method:
+    def __init__(self, handle, name):
+        self.handle, self.name = handle, name
+
+    async def remote(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        self.handle.calls.append((self.handle.label, self.name, kwargs.get("global_steps", args[0] if args else None)))
+        return self.handle.results.get(self.name, True)
+
+
+class _Handle:
+    """Stands in for a Ray actor handle and records calls in a shared log."""
+
+    def __init__(self, label, calls, results=None):
+        self.label, self.calls, self.results = label, calls, results or {}
+
+    def __getattr__(self, name):
+        return _Method(self, name)
+
+
+def _manifest(version):
+    return WeightManifest(version=version, endpoint=b"", total_bytes=0, tensors=[], buckets=[])
+
+
+def _agent(registry, calls, worker_results=None, **kwargs):
+    servers = [_Handle("server0", calls), _Handle("server1", calls)]
+    workers = [_Handle("worker0", calls, worker_results), _Handle("worker1", calls, worker_results)]
+    return WeightUpdateAgent(servers, workers, registry=registry, poll_interval=0.01, **kwargs)
+
+
+async def _run_until(agent, version):
+    task = asyncio.create_task(agent.run())
+    try:
+        return await agent.wait_for_version(version, timeout=5)
+    finally:
+        agent.stop()
+        await task
+

+        assert await _run_until(agent, 3) == 3
+
+        names = [name for _, name, _ in calls]
+        # Prefetch runs while generation continues; everything after abort is the pause.
+        assert names == [
+            "prefetch_weights",
+            "prefetch_weights",
+            "abort_all_requests",
+            "abort_all_requests",
+            "wait_for_requests_to_drain",
+            "release_kv_cache",
+            "release_kv_cache",
+            "update_weights",
+            "update_weights",
+            "resume_kv_cache",
+            "resume_kv_cache",
+            "resume_engine_generation",
+            "open_submission_gate",
+            "open_submission_gate",
+        ]
+        assert {v for _, name, v in calls if name in ("prefetch_weights", "update_weights")} == {3}
+        assert [
+            label for label, name, _ in calls if name in ("wait_for_requests_to_drain", "resume_engine_generation")
+        ] == [
+            "server0",
+            "server0",
+        ]

+def test_resume_resets_inflight_prompts_to_pending(tq_init):

+    statuses = {"pending": None, "running": None, "finished": None}
+    for status in statuses:

+        statuses[status] = uid
+        batch = tu.get_tensordict({"uid": [uid], "index": torch.tensor([0])})
+        tag = {"is_prompt": True, "status": status, "global_steps": 2, "min_weight_version": 1}
+        tq.kv_batch_put(keys=[uid], partition_id=partition_id, tags=[tag], fields=batch)

+    for status in ("running", "finished"):

+    assert _stub(global_steps=7, published_version=6)._reissue_inflight_prompts(partition_id) == 2

+    tags = _prompt_tags(partition_id)
+    for status in ("pending", "running"):
+        tag = tags[statuses[status]]
+        assert tag["status"] == "pending" and tag["global_steps"] == 7 and tag["min_weight_version"] == 6

+
+import asyncio
+import uuid
+
+import pytest
+import torch

+

+def tq_init():
+    tq.init()
+    yield
+    tq.close()
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def partition_id(monkeypatch):
+    # The dispatcher calls tq.init() as a Ray actor would; the module fixture already did.
+    monkeypatch.setattr(prompt_dispatcher.tq, "init", lambda *args, **kwargs: None)
+    return f"test-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
+
+
+class _Remote:
+    def __init__(self, fn):
+        self.fn = fn
+
+    async def remote(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        return self.fn(*args, **kwargs)
+
+
+class _Worker:
+    """Records the uids and global_steps of every batch it is asked to generate."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.batches = []
+        self.generate_sequences = _Remote(
+            lambda batch: self.batches.append((list(batch["uid"]), tu.get_non_tensor_data(batch, "global_steps", None)))
+        )
+
+    @property
+    def uids(self):
+        return [uid for uids, _ in self.batches for uid in uids]
+
+
+class _Agent:
+    def __init__(self, version=0, failed=False):
+        self.version, self.failed = version, failed
+        self.get_state = _Remote(lambda: {"version": self.version, "failed": self.failed})
+
+
+def _enqueue(partition_id, global_steps, min_weight_version, n=1):
+    uids = [uuid.uuid4().hex for _ in range(n)]
+    batch = tu.get_tensordict({"uid": uids, "index": torch.arange(n)})
+    tag = {
+        "is_prompt": True,
+        "status": "pending",
+        "global_steps": global_steps,
+        "min_weight_version": min_weight_version,
+    }
+    tq.kv_batch_put(keys=uids, partition_id=partition_id, tags=[dict(tag) for _ in uids], fields=batch)
+    return uids
+
+
+def _set_status(partition_id, uids, status):
+    tq.kv_batch_put(keys=uids, partition_id=partition_id, tags=[{"status": status} for _ in uids])
+
+
+def _dispatcher(partition_id, workers, agents, **kwargs):
+    return PromptDispatcher(workers, agents, partition_id=partition_id, poll_interval=0.01, **kwargs)
+
+
+def test_waits_until_every_replica_has_the_required_version(tq_init, partition_id):
+    async def main():
+        workers, agents = [_Worker()], [_Agent(version=1), _Agent(version=0)]
+        dispatcher = _dispatcher(partition_id, workers, agents)
+        old = _enqueue(partition_id, global_steps=1, min_weight_version=0)
+        new = _enqueue(partition_id, global_steps=2, min_weight_version=1)
+
+        assert await dispatcher.dispatch_once() == 1
+        assert workers[0].uids == old
+        assert dispatcher.get_state()["waiting_for_version"] == 1
+
+        # Polling again must not start the claimed prompt twice, even though it is still pending.
+        assert await dispatcher.dispatch_once() == 0
+
+        agents[1].version = 1
+        assert await dispatcher.dispatch_once() == 1
+        assert workers[0].uids == old + new
+
+    asyncio.run(main())
+
+
+def test_caps_inflight_and_claims_oldest_first(tq_init, partition_id):
+    async def main():
+        workers = [_Worker()]
+        dispatcher = _dispatcher(partition_id, workers, [_Agent(version=5)], max_inflight_prompts=2)
+        late = _enqueue(partition_id, global_steps=3, min_weight_version=0, n=2)
+        early = _enqueue(partition_id, global_steps=1, min_weight_version=0, n=2)
+
+        assert await dispatcher.dispatch_once() == 2
+        assert sorted(workers[0].uids) == sorted(early)
+        assert workers[0].batches[0][1] == 1, "the batch carries the steps the prompts were enqueued at"
+
+        # Running prompts still count toward the cap; finished ones free a slot.
+        _set_status(partition_id, early, "running")
+        assert await dispatcher.dispatch_once() == 0
+        _set_status(partition_id, early[:1], "finished")
+        assert await dispatcher.dispatch_once() == 1
+        assert workers[0].uids[-1] in late
+        assert dispatcher.get_state()["inflight"] == 2
+
+    asyncio.run(main())
+
+
+def test_spreads_batches_over_workers(tq_init, partition_id):
+    async def main():
+        workers = [_Worker(), _Worker(), _Worker()]
+        dispatcher = _dispatcher(partition_id, workers, [_Agent()])
+        for step in range(4):
+            _enqueue(partition_id, global_steps=step, min_weight_version=0)
+            await dispatcher.dispatch_once()
+        # One prompt per poll, rotating so the first worker does not get them all.
+        assert [len(worker.uids) for worker in workers] == [2, 1, 1]
+
+    asyncio.run(main())
+
+
+def test_failed_update_agent_stops_dispatch(tq_init, partition_id):
+    async def main():
+        dispatcher = _dispatcher(partition_id, [_Worker()], [_Agent(), _Agent(failed=True)])
+        _enqueue(partition_id, global_steps=1, min_weight_version=0)
+        task = asyncio.create_task(dispatcher.run())
+        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="weight update agent failed"):
+            await asyncio.wait_for(task, timeout=5)
+        assert dispatcher.get_state()["failed"]
+
+    asyncio.run(main())

+"""A WeightUpdateAgent keeps a real vLLM replica on the newest published weights, under load.
+
+The test process publishes three versions: the original weights, then weights whose final norm is
+zeroed (so every logit is 0 and greedy decoding degenerates), then the original weights again.
+Greedy outputs show which weights the replica serves, and every output reports its weight version.
+
+Usage:
+    pytest tests/workers/rollout/rollout_vllm/test_vllm_weight_update_agent.py -v -s
+"""
+
+import asyncio
+import os
+from uuid import uuid4
+
+import pytest
+import ray
+import torch
+
+MODEL_PATH = os.path.expanduser(os.getenv("WEIGHT_UPDATE_AGENT_TEST_MODEL", "~/models/Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct"))
+GREEDY = {"temperature": 0.0, "top_p": 1.0, "logprobs": False}
+
+
+def _rollout_config():
+    from hydra import compose, initialize_config_dir
+
+    config_dir = os.path.abspath("verl/trainer/config")
+    with initialize_config_dir(config_dir=config_dir, version_base=None):
+        config = compose(config_name="ppo_trainer")
+    config.actor_rollout_ref.model.path = MODEL_PATH
+    rollout = config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout
+    rollout.name = "vllm"
+    rollout.mode = "async"
+    rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size = 1
+    rollout.prompt_length = 256
+    rollout.response_length = 512
+    rollout.gpu_memory_utilization = 0.5
+    rollout.load_format = "auto"
+    rollout.checkpoint_engine.backend = "transport_pull"
+    rollout.checkpoint_engine.update_weights_bucket_megabytes = 256
+    return config.actor_rollout_ref
+
+
+def _versions():
+    """Original weights, weights with the final norm zeroed, original weights again."""
+    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
+
+    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(MODEL_PATH, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    original = [(name, tensor.detach().clone()) for name, tensor in model.state_dict().items()]
+    broken = [(name, torch.zeros_like(t) if name == "model.norm.weight" else t) for name, t in original]
+    assert any(name == "model.norm.weight" for name, _ in original)
+    return [original, broken, original]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not os.path.isdir(MODEL_PATH), reason=f"{MODEL_PATH} not found")
+def test_agent_updates_vllm_replica_under_load():
+    pytest.importorskip("nixl")
+    ray.init(ignore_reinit_error=True, runtime_env={"env_vars": {"VLLM_USE_V1": "1"}})
+    try:
+        asyncio.run(_run())
+    finally:
+        ray.shutdown()
+
+
+async def _run():
+    from transformers import AutoTokenizer
+
+    from verl.checkpoint_engine.transport import RayWeightRegistry
+    from verl.checkpoint_engine.transport.publisher import WeightPublisher
+    from verl.checkpoint_engine.transport.update_agent import WeightUpdateAgent
+    from verl.utils.tokenizer import normalize_token_ids
+    from verl.workers.rollout.replica import get_rollout_replica_class
+
+    actor_rollout_ref = _rollout_config()
+    replica = get_rollout_replica_class("vllm")(
+        replica_rank=0, config=actor_rollout_ref.rollout, model_config=actor_rollout_ref.model, gpus_per_node=1
+    )
+    await replica.init_standalone()
+    server = replica.servers[0]
+
+    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_PATH)
+    prompt_ids = normalize_token_ids(
+        tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
+            [{"role": "user", "content": "Name three primary colors."}], add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=True
+        )
+    )
+

+"""Checkpoint engine adapter for publish/pull weight sync.
+
+This lets the publisher and puller run inside today's CheckpointEngineManager flow: the trainer's
+`send_weights` publishes a version and every rollout worker's `receive_weights` pulls it. There is
+no topology and no per-step setup, since endpoints and descriptors travel through the registry.
+Rollout-driven pulls without the manager build on the same publisher and puller.
+"""
+
+import logging
+import os
+from typing import AsyncGenerator, Generator
+
+import torch
+
+from verl.checkpoint_engine.base import CheckpointEngine, CheckpointEngineRegistry
+
+from .puller import TornReadError, WeightPuller
+from .registry import LeaseError, RayWeightRegistry
+from .transport import TransportFactory, default_transport_factory
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+logger.setLevel(os.getenv("VERL_LOGGING_LEVEL", "WARN"))
+
+
+@CheckpointEngineRegistry.register("transport_pull")
+class TransportPullCheckpointEngine(CheckpointEngine):
+    """Trainer rank 0 publishes weight versions; rollout workers pull them with one-sided reads.
+
+    The default transport, "nixl_native", runs on any torch. torch.distributed._transport backends
+    need torch >= 2.15 on both trainer and rollout, since the two transports cannot interoperate.
+
+    Args:
+        bucket_size: Size in bytes of one remote read.
+        device: Device of the publisher slots and puller mirror. "cpu" (pinned host memory) by
+            default: each slot holds a full model copy, which rarely fits next to training state.
+        transport: Transport backend: "nixl_native" (any torch), or a torch.distributed._transport
+            backend such as "nixl" (torch >= 2.15). Not named `backend`, which selects the engine.
+        num_slots: Versions the publisher keeps at once.
+        rollout_dtype: dtype fp32 weights are cast to before publishing, e.g. torch.bfloat16 or
+            "bfloat16"; None sends them as the trainer produces them.
+        lease_ttl: Reader lease duration in seconds.
+        registry_name: Ray actor name of the shared registry.
+        wait_timeout: Seconds a rollout worker waits for the requested version to be published.
+        is_master: Whether this is trainer rank 0, the only publisher.
+        transport_factory: Override of transport construction, for tests.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        bucket_size: int,
+        device: str = "cpu",
+        transport: str = "nixl_native",
+        num_slots: int = 2,
+        rollout_dtype: torch.dtype | str | None = torch.bfloat16,
+        lease_ttl: float = 60.0,
+        registry_name: str = "verl_weight_registry",
+        wait_timeout: float = 600.0,
+        is_master: bool = False,
+        transport_factory: TransportFactory = default_transport_factory,
+    ):
+        self.bucket_size = bucket_size
+        self.device = device
+        self.transport = transport
+        self.num_slots = num_slots
+        self.rollout_dtype = getattr(torch, rollout_dtype) if isinstance(rollout_dtype, str) else rollout_dtype
+        self.lease_ttl = lease_ttl
+        self.registry_name = registry_name
+        self.wait_timeout = wait_timeout
+        self.is_master = is_master
+        self.transport_factory = transport_factory
+        self._registry = None
+        self.publisher = None
+        self.puller = None
+        self._prefetched = None
+        # Last version published (trainer) or pulled (rollout) by this engine.
+        self.last_version = -1
+
+    @property
+    def registry(self):
+        if self._registry is None:
+            self._registry = RayWeightRegistry(name=self.registry_name)
+        return self._registry
+
+    def prepare(self) -> dict:
+        return {}
+
+    @classmethod
+    def build_topology(cls, actor_wg_world_size: int, rollout_world_size: int, metadata: list[dict]):
+        return {}, {}
+
+    def init_process_group(self, **kwargs):
+        pass
+
+    def finalize(self):
+        # Slots and registrations live across steps; that is what makes per-step setup unnecessary.
+        pass
+
+    @torch.no_grad()
+    async def send_weights(
+        self,
+        weights: Generator[tuple[str, torch.Tensor], None, None],
+        global_steps: int | None = None,
+    ):
+        """Publish the weights as version `global_steps` (trainer rank 0 only).
+
+        Without `global_steps` the version is one past the last published one. A version that was
+        already published is not published again.
+        """
+        version = global_steps if global_steps is not None else self.last_version + 1
+        if not self.is_master or version <= self.last_version:
+            # Every rank still drains the generator: gathering full tensors is collective.
+            for _ in weights:
+                pass
+            return
+        if self.publisher is None:
+            from .publisher import WeightPublisher
+
+            self.publisher = WeightPublisher(
+                self.registry,
+                self.bucket_size,
+                device=self.device,
+                backend=self.transport,
+                num_slots=self.num_slots,
+                rollout_dtype=self.rollout_dtype,
+                transport_factory=self.transport_factory,
+            )
+        await self.publisher.publish(weights, version=version)
+        self.last_version = version
+
+    def _get_puller(self) -> WeightPuller:
+        if self.puller is None:
+            self.puller = WeightPuller(
+                self.registry,
+                device=self.device,
+                backend=self.transport,
+                lease_ttl=self.lease_ttl,
+                transport_factory=self.transport_factory,
+            )
+        return self.puller
+
+    async def prefetch(self, version: int) -> bool:
+        """Pull `version` into the local mirror without touching the inference engine.
+
+        Rollout can keep generating meanwhile; the next `receive_weights` hands out the prefetched
+        copy instead of reading again.
+
+        Returns:
+            False if the version was retired or the read was torn, so the caller should retry with
+            a newer version.
+        """
+        manifest = await self.registry.get_manifest(version)
+        if manifest is None:
+            return False
+        try:
+            self._prefetched = await self._get_puller().fetch(manifest)
+        except (LeaseError, TornReadError) as e:
+            logger.warning(f"Prefetch of version {version} failed: {e}")
+            return False
+        return True
+
+    @torch.no_grad()
+    async def receive_weights(self, global_steps: int | None = None) -> AsyncGenerator[tuple[str, torch.Tensor], None]:
+        """Yield the newest version that is at least `global_steps`, or newer than the last one.
+
+        A version taken by `prefetch` is used when it is new enough; otherwise it is pulled now.
+        """
+        min_version = global_steps if global_steps is not None else self.last_version + 1
+        pulled, self._prefetched = self._prefetched, None
+        while pulled is None or pulled.version < min_version:
+            manifest = await self._get_puller().wait_for_version(min_version, timeout=self.wait_timeout)
+            try:
+                pulled = await self.puller.fetch(manifest)
+            except (LeaseError, TornReadError) as e:
+                # Retired before it could be leased, or the lease lapsed mid-read: a newer version
+                # is already READY, so start over from the latest one.
+                logger.warning(f"Pull of version {manifest.version} failed, retrying: {e}")
+                pulled = None
+        self.last_version = pulled.version
+        for name, tensor in pulled.named_tensors():
+            yield name, tensor
